notes: SMR (hold on tender spot), static vs dynamic stretching, drawing-in (TVA) vs bracing (global co-contraction), and balance progressions (smaller base, less stable surface, eyes closed) match commonly described NASM content.
No wording appears copied from NASM materials.

4/2/1 tempo = 4 s eccentric, 2 s isometric, 1 s concentric matches NASM convention. 'Lowering' is a plain-English stand-in for eccentric; for pulling moves (rows, pulldowns) the eccentric is the return phase. Optional wording improvement: 'lowering (eccentric) / pause / lifting (concentric)'. Not counted as an error.
Push-up regression/progression examples, broomstick neutral-spine check (head, upper back, tailbone), exhale-on-effort are correct.
Visual/auditory/kinesthetic cue definitions, spotting (stay close, agree on reps beforehand, watch bar/wrists), and stop-on-pain/form-breakdown are consistent with NASM spotting guidance.

5 phases / 3 levels (1, 3, 1) correct. Phase 1 12-20 reps slow tempo; Phase 4 1-5 reps, 3-5 min rest; Phase 3 hypertrophy; Phase 5 strength+power superset (bench press + medicine ball chest pass, squat + squat jump) all match the OPT model as commonly described.
Phase 2 example (bench press then stability ball push-up) is the standard strength/stabilization superset example; correct.
OPT names are NASM terminology (necessary for the exam); sentences themselves are original plain English.
Acute variables listed with 'include' (NASM list is longer: volume, frequency, duration too) - not wrong.
GAS stages alarm reaction / resistance development / exhaustion match NASM naming; SAID and progressive overload correct.

HHS PAG 2nd ed. (2018) is still the current edition; the 3rd edition is expected in 2028. Adults: 150-300 min moderate (or 75-150 vigorous) + muscle-strengthening 2+ days. 'At least 150 minutes of moderate' is a correct simplification (vigorous alternative omitted). Evidence: https://odphp.health.gov/news/202410/get-involved-contribute-next-edition-physical-activity-guidelines , https://www.cdc.gov/physical-activity-basics/guidelines/adults.html

Talk test (talk not sing = moderate; few words = vigorous) matches CDC. Stage I = aerobic base, later stages add intervals; FITTE with Enjoyment; Corrective Exercise Continuum order inhibit-lengthen-activate-integrate all correct.
PAR-Q+, medical clearance, objective vs subjective data, screen-and-refer are correct.
Karvonen example verified: (180-70) x 0.6 + 70 = 136 bpm; %HRmax 180 x 0.6 = 108 bpm. BMI 70 / 1.75^2 = 22.86 -> 22.9. All arithmetic correct.

CDC adult BMI categories (<18.5, 18.5 to <25, 25 to <30, >=30) confirmed; CDC page last updated March 19, 2024, so source year 2024 is correct. Evidence: https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
220 - age is presented as 'a common estimate', which is true. NASM 7th edition also uses 208 - (0.7 x age) for zone setting; optional to mention, not an error.
Rockport: estimate also uses age, sex, and body weight; text says time and ending HR are 'used' - incomplete but not false.

OHSA compensations: knees in (adductors, TFL over; glute medius under), low back arches (hip flexors over; glutes, core under), arms fall forward (lats, pecs over; mid/lower traps, rhomboids under) match the NASM tables as commonly described (lists are partial with 'likely', acceptable).
Upper/lower crossed syndrome descriptions correct.
Planes and examples (lateral raise frontal, wood chop transverse) correct; muscle roles, contraction types, spindle (length/rate) vs GTO (tension, relaxation) correct.
ATP-PC ~10 s, glycolysis up to ~2 min, oxidative for longer work are consistent with NASM/standard exercise-physiology texts.
Tip 'Power for a Couple of seconds' is loose (ATP-PC lasts up to ~10 s) but the definition right above states 10 s; optional to reword as 'Power for a few seconds'.
Cardiac output = HR x SV and lower resting HR with aerobic training are correct.
4-4-9 kcal/g, ADEK fat-soluble, C and B water-soluble, carbohydrate as main high-intensity fuel, 3,500 kcal/lb flagged as rule of thumb - all correct.
General coaching content; nothing factually wrong.
SMART expansion is one accepted variant (NASM also uses 'Timely'); stages of change order and descriptions correct.
Scope of practice, referral, general nutrition only, confidentiality correct.
AHA 2025 Guidelines (Part 7 Adult BLS) keep compression rate 100-120/min, full recoil, depth 2-2.4 in. Source year 2025 correct. Evidence: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001369
Call 911 - CPR - AED sequence correct.
